title: Timeout Bootstrapping for Long-CoT RLVR: Promise and Pitfalls

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to systematize how truncation of long chain-of-thought (CoT) rollouts is handled in RLVR training. Paper [1] discusses RL training design choices for long CoT reasoning but does not specifically address truncation handling strategies. Paper [3] mentions challenges in extending RLVR to reasoning-intensive domains but does not focus on truncation handling. Paper [8] discusses truncating trajectories in Monte Carlo RL but focuses on fixed-length episodes rather than systematic strategies for handling truncation in long CoT rollouts. Paper [24] provides a formal account of handling time limits in RL but does not address truncation strategies specific to RLVR or CoT reasoning. No prior paper explicitly systematizes truncation handling in RLVR training.

### Mechanism
The contribution formalizes three truncation handling strategies: truncate-as-failure, DAPO overlong shaping, and timeout bootstrapping from the critic's value estimate. Paper [8] discusses truncating trajectories in Monte Carlo RL but does not cover these specific strategies. Paper [10] provides mathematical insights into DAPO but does not address truncation handling. Paper [24] discusses time limits in RL but does not formalize truncation strategies like those in this contribution. Paper [22] mentions bootstrapping in value learning but does not apply it to truncation handling in RLVR. None of the prior papers formalize the same mechanisms.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates truncation handling strategies through systematic comparison on long-horizon mathematical reasoning with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B. Paper [2] uses DeepSeek-R1 for reasoning tasks but does not systematically compare truncation handling strategies. Paper [14] evaluates RL training recipes for reasoning but does not focus on truncation handling. Paper [12] uses BFS-PO for reasoning tasks but does not evaluate truncation strategies. Paper [9] addresses rollout inefficiencies in RLVR but does not evaluate truncation handling. No prior paper uses the same evaluation design for truncation handling strategies.

### Domain
The contribution operates in RLVR training for long-CoT reasoning. Paper [3] explicitly addresses RLVR for long-CoT reasoning, as does paper [7]. Paper [6] discusses RL methods for long-horizon tasks, including reasoning. Paper [17] addresses RL algorithms for reasoning tasks, including long-CoT reasoning. The domain is covered by prior work.
